chapter: Chicago friends: Tesch, Stacy and Wettling
title: A 96-year-old New Orleans bassist and his chick of 78
summary: Freeman tells a story of an elderly New Orleans bassist on a London tour, and jokes about forgetting names.

story.theme_name: Band pranks, jokes and gigs gone wrong
story.community_name: Pranks, practical jokes and band humor

blocks.x: A very, very funny story, if I may throw this in, speaking about men who are still around playing well in their eighties and maybe a couple in their nineties, there was a bass player from New Orleans that was doing a show with a New Orleans band and I think his name is Russell, I am not positive of the name now, because I did not meet him, but this was the story I heard.
He was here in London, and I think he was in his

nineties -- would it be incredible to say he was about 96 and he was doing some one-nighters with this band and the English road manager, when they got to London, may I help you into your hotel room and the guy said, 'Oh, thanks, man, but I'm okay. I got my chick with me.' His chick is 78.
I am terribly sorry, I can't remember the man's name. Garland or something, oh, dear.
I am that way about names. I must tell you, Helen, a funny thing about names. I had an uncle who had the same name as I and I remember I was introducing him many years ago and I forgot his name.
That's hard to top that one.
